aboutMeContent: Junior Software Developer, with a completed german IHK qualification as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
aboutMeContent2: After several years in IT (as a technician), I discovered my passion for software development, through a retraining program as an Computer Science Expert: Software Development as well as through hands-on experience in various projects and internships.
aboutMeContent3: During my retraining, I focused mainly on C# and MySQL, from console applications to small GUI projects using WinForms and WPF. During my internship, I gained my first hands-on experience with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, including frameworks and tools like EJS, React.js, Bootstrap, and Node.js. My final project at the end of the program was a web application for automating phone number provider switches, implemented using the React framework Next.js.
aboutMeContent4: In addition to the IHK certification as an Computer Science Expert: Software Development, I also earned the Professional Scrum Master I, ITIL® Foundation in IT Service Management, and the GPM Basic Certificate in Project Management during my retraining.
aboutMeContent5: What sets me apart: I don’t give up. Even when the conditions aren’t ideal, I find ways to keep learning, through online courses, personal projects, or simply by trying things out. I quickly adapt to new tools, enjoy thinking in solutions, and love writing code that simplifies real-world processes.
aboutMeContent6: I’m looking for a team where I can grow, both technically and personally. The rest? You’ll see in the code.

project1.title: PDF2FORM
project1.title2: A web-based porting tool for provider change orders
project1.description: As part of my final examination to become a Computer Science Expert for Software Development, I developed a web application to automate phone number provider change processes. The goal was to replace manual, error-prone procedures with an efficient, semi-automated solution.
project1.description2: Using Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Prisma, and MySQL, I implemented a complete frontend and backend system. Through a modern interface, users can input data, which is automatically validated, stored in a relational database, and transferred into PDF forms. The app enables centralized tracking, clear validations, and seamless PDF generation.
project1.description3: I was responsible for the entire technical concept, including database modeling, API logic, UI design, and integration. The application was successfully deployed on Terrera AG’s servers and handed over for productive use. The project work also included documentation for the IHK and internal users.
project1.description4: This project allowed me to practically deepen my knowledge in full-stack development, data modeling, and application security, and was an important step in my professional development.

project2.title: Your Anime Persona
project2.title2: An Anime Web Application with Public API
project2.description: This project was created during my retraining internship while completing the Udemy course 'The Complete Full-Stack Web Development Bootcamp'. It is a web application built with Node.js, Express.js, EJS, and Bootstrap, and it integrates a public API (Jikan API).
project2.description2: The application allows users to enter the name of an anime series and randomly displays a character from that series. HTTP GET requests are made using Axios.
project2.description3: The project was primarily for learning purposes and runs both locally and on a hosted server.
project2.description4: The application was entirely written by me and developed as a self-study exercise (not related to the company’s work).
project2.imageAlt: Screenshot of Your Anime Persona application

project3.title: The Tiny Blogs
project3.description: This project was created during my retraining internship while completing the Udemy course 'The Complete Full-Stack Web Development Bootcamp'. It is a simple blog web application developed using Node.js, Express.js, EJS, and Bootstrap. The application allows users to create, edit, delete, and view blog posts.
project3.description2: Since no database is used, posts are not retained across sessions. The application was developed mainly for learning purposes and tested both locally and on a hosted server.
project3.description3: The content on the live site can be modified by anyone, as no authentication is implemented.
project3.description4: The project was entirely written by me and developed as a self-study exercise (not related to the company’s work).
project3.imageAlt: Screenshot of The Tiny Blogs application

project4.title: Personal Site
project4.description: This project was created during my retraining internship while completing the Udemy course 'The Complete Full-Stack Web Development Bootcamp'. The website is a simple, responsive personal site built with HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap, and is intended to showcase my background and some of my previous projects as an aspiring developer.
project4.description2: The website also includes a linked online resume and a small portfolio assignment. Both were created using only HTML and were part of the course.
project4.description3: The content and projects reflect the status at the time of creation, as this is a learning project and no regular updates are planned.
project4.description4: The application was entirely written by me and developed as a self-study exercise (not related to the company’s work).
project4.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Personal Site website

project5.title: Andreas & Daniel
project5.title2: A Responsive Website as a Collaborative Project
project5.description: A small web project I developed during my web development retraining internship. In the newer version, the site was redesigned to be responsive. It was rebuilt using a modern Flexbox layout and media queries to ensure a better user experience across different screen sizes.
project5.description2: The first version was built using only HTML and CSS and reflected my creative approach to web design. The goal was to strengthen and apply basic frontend development skills in a practical way.
project5.description3: This project helped me deepen my hands-on knowledge of responsive web design, Flexbox, and CSS layout techniques.
project5.description4: The application was fully developed independently by me together with a colleague as a self-study exercise (not related to the company’s work).
project5.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Andreas & Daniel website

project6.title: Snake
project6.title2: A Revised Remake of the Classic Snake Game
project6.description: A Java project created as part of my trial project during the retraining to become a Computer Science Expert: Software Development. It is a version of the classic Snake game with a graphical user interface (JavaFX). The goal of the game is to control the snake across the field and collect as many points as possible without running into itself.
project6.description2: The main challenges were using JavaFX for the first time and integrating the functionality within Eclipse.
project6.description3: The project was originally based on a YouTube tutorial, which I used as the foundation for implementing the game. I rebuilt the source code, fully understood it, and then made my own adjustments and enhancements.

project7.title: My Learn Plan
project7.title2: A Learning Plan Application for Weekly Organization
project7.description: 'My Learn Plan' is an application developed with C# WPF. It allows users to record daily learning goals for each week. The entered notes are saved automatically and reloaded the next time the program is opened – ideal for exam preparation or tracking retraining content.
project7.description2: The project was created on my own initiative during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project7.imageAlt: Screenshot of the My Learn Plan application

project8.title: Startup Motivational Message
project8.description: A simple Python script that displays a randomly selected, self-written motivational message in a graphical window every time the system starts. This project was created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development, with the goal of motivating myself each morning before studying or programming.
project8.description2: The implementation uses Python's tkinter module to display a GUI message with rotating motivational quotes. The script runs quietly in the background without a terminal window and can be launched automatically via the Windows Task Scheduler or the Startup folder.
project8.description3: The code was written entirely by me.
project8.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Startup Motivational Message script

project9.title: Presence Days Calculator
project9.title2: A Tool for Calculating Retraining Attendance Days
project9.description: A practical tool for calculating the required attendance days according to IHK guidelines, developed with Windows Forms in C#. It was created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project9.description2: According to the IHK, at least 51% of the training days must be attended in person. This application allows users to enter the attended days for each month, automatically calculates the total, and shows how many days are still missing. Additionally, it includes a save and load feature to retain the data.
project9.description3: The project was originally developed for personal use but turned out to be very helpful and also served as a learning project.
project9.description4: The code was written entirely by me.
project9.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Presence Days Calculator application

project10.title: Cioco's Homepage
project10.description: This small web application is my personal start page, where I organized frequently visited websites into categories such as 'Social', 'News', 'IT', 'Gaming', and 'Shopping'.
project10.description2: It also includes a clock, a Google search bar, and a responsive design.
project10.description3: The project was created as a practice exercise using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and was inspired by a trainer’s homepage during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project10.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Cioco's Homepage website

project11.title: No Guts
project11.title2: A Text-Based Decision Game with Humor
project11.description: This final project was created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development. Later, the project was expanded, revised, and completely rewritten.
project11.description2: 'No Guts', later renamed 'Still No Guts', is a humorous choose-your-own-adventure game in which the player makes decisions that influence the protagonist's self-esteem. Depending on the self-esteem level, the story, dialogues, and even the endings change.
project11.description3: The revised version includes additional content, more branching paths, ASCII art, improved structure, colored console output, and was fully translated into English.
project11.description4: The code was written entirely by me.
project11.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Still No Guts game application

project12.title: Palindrom
project12.description: A C# WPF project for detecting palindromes. The application checks whether an entered word or sentence is a palindrome—i.e., it reads the same forwards and backwards. All non-letter characters are ignored, and the check is case-insensitive. The user interface includes a freely usable background image.
project12.description2: It was my first WPF project and was created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project12.description3: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.

project13.title: Ein-Aus Knopf
project13.description: A small C# Windows Forms project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development. The application simulates a switch that can only toggle between the states 'OFF' and 'ON' by entering a predefined code ('123456'). The window can only be closed when the application is in the 'ON' state.
project13.description2: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.
project13.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Ein-Aus Knopf application

project14.title: 5 in 1
project14.title2: A Console Tool with Five Small Programs
project14.description: This C# console application project was developed as part of my training to become a Computer Science Expert: Software Development. The application offers a menu with five different programs the user can choose from:
project14.description4: **Fibonacci:** In the Fibonacci sequence, each number is the sum of the two preceding ones.
project14.description5: **Calculator:** A basic calculator for arithmetic operations.
project14.description6: **Warm and Colder:** A number guessing game.
project14.description7: Older or revised versions of some of these programs (by me) are available on GitHub. Bubblesort, Fibonacci, and the calculator each have an earlier version. There is also a newer WinForms version of the calculator and an improved version of the 'Warm and Colder' game with a high score feature.
project14.description8: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.
project14.link3Alt: GitHub Repository (Warm und Kälter - newer Version)

project15.title: Caesar Cipher
project15.title2: An Encryption Tool with JSON Export
project15.description: A C# Windows Forms project implementing the classic Caesar cipher encryption method. The application was created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development. Users can encrypt and decrypt text (with a fixed offset of +2). Additionally, encrypted words can be saved in JSON format and loaded again later.
project15.description2: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.
project15.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Caesar Cipher application

project16.title: Die Bücherei
project16.title2: A Console Project Simulating a Library System
project16.description: A C# console app practice project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development. The application simulates a library system where various media types such as books, software, and videos can be borrowed and returned.
project16.description2: The project demonstrates the use of object-oriented programming (inheritance, method overriding, class structure) as well as the management of customers and their media loans, including return deadlines and reviews.
project16.description3: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.
project16.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Die Bücherei application

project17.title: Nutzer
project17.title2: A Console Tool for Managing User Profiles
project17.description: A C# console app practice project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project17.description2: The program allows users to create, display, save, and load user profiles containing first name, last name, and date of birth. The data is serialized and deserialized using XML.
project17.description3: It was my first practical introduction to working with XML files in C# and to handling user interaction through a console menu.
project17.description4: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.

project18.title: Bits & Bites
project18.title2: An Order System with Discount Logic for a Fictional Store
project18.description: A C# console app practice project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project18.description2: The program simulates orders for drinks, food, and internet tickets in a fictional store and demonstrates the use of polymorphism, class hierarchies, and discount calculation.
project18.description3: Note: The program is not intended to be interactive, but rather serves as a simulation with predefined data to illustrate object-oriented logic.
project18.description4: Various discount logics are taken into account, such as a 'Happy Hour' for alcoholic beverages, surcharges for large portions, and a 5% discount for holders of the 'Bits & Bites' card.
project18.description5: The focus is on object-oriented programming using inheritance and polymorphism.
project18.description6: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.
project18.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Bits & Bites application

project19.title: Tierverwaltung
project19.description: A C# console app practice project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development at Lutz + Grub Academy. The program simulates the management of animals in a system, allowing new animals to be added and various attributes such as name, weight, and species to be managed.
project19.description2: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.

project20.title: Rechnerverwaltung
project20.title2: A Text-Based Application for Managing Computer Types
project20.description: A C# console app practice project created as part of my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project20.description2: The program is used to manage different types of computers within a company network, including servers, office workstations, graphics-intensive workstations, and terminals.
project20.description3: The project uses object-oriented principles such as inheritance and polymorphism to efficiently represent and manage the different device types.
project20.description4: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.

project21.description: A C# console app practice project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development. The project simulates a document filing system in which the user can view and manage information about specific documents.
project21.description2: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.

The program allows for the management and storage of address data, including street, house number, city, and postal code. It can also process customer data such as name, date of birth, and credit rating.
project22.description2: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.

project23.title: Zoo-Programm

project23.description: A C# console app practice project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development at Lutz + Grub Academy. The program simulates an automated information booth for a small zoo.
project23.description2: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.

project24.title: Wassermelone
project24.title2: A Discount Simulation for Watermelon Sales
project24.description: A C# console app practice project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development at Lutz + Grub Academy. It simulates a receipt for the purchase of watermelons, applying discounts based on quantity and day of the week.
project24.description2: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.

project25.title: Don’t Feed The Trolls
project25.description: A simple HTML and CSS project assignment created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development at Lutz + Grub Academy. This was my first project in web development, where I created a basic website featuring an image, text, and a link to another page.
project25.description2: The code was written entirely by me.
project25.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Don’t Feed The Trolls website

project26.title: Fahrzeughandel
project26.title2: A Simulation of a Virtual Vehicle Dealership
project26.description: A C# console app practice project developed during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project26.description2: The application simulates a small vehicle dealership. Vehicles are stored and assigned to specific test drives. For each test drive, it is randomly determined whether a vehicle was sold; sold vehicles are then removed from the available list.
project26.description3: The project uses object-oriented programming to model vehicles and test drives.
project26.description4: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.

project27.title: Tarifrechner
project27.title2: A Virtual Rate Calculator for Phone Costs
project27.description: A C# console app practice project developed during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project27.description2: The application compares landline and mobile phone plans based on predefined rate data. The user enters how many minutes they talk per month and receives a cost calculation for different plans.
project27.description3: The project is based on object-oriented programming with multiple classes for modeling rates and includes simple selection and calculation logic.
project27.description4: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.

project28.title: Kaffeemaschine
project28.title2: A Simulation of a Coffee Machine
project28.description: A C# console app practice project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project28.description2: This was my first object-oriented programming (OOP) project. The app simulates a coffee machine with functions for refilling water and beans, as well as dispensing coffee.
project28.description3: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.

project29.title: Lotto
project29.title2: A Simulation of a Lottery Game
project29.description: A simple C# console app practice project developed during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project29.description2: The app simulates a lottery game: six random numbers between 1 and 49 are drawn, and the user also enters six numbers.
project29.description3: At the end, the app shows how many matches were achieved.
project29.description4: The code was written entirely by me.

project30.title: Schere, Stein, Papier
project30.title2: A Console Game with Random Decisions
project30.description: A simple C# console app practice project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project30.description2: The user competes against the computer in the classic game 'Rock, Paper, Scissors'. The computer's choice is random, and the outcome is determined by comparing both inputs.
project30.description3: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.

project31.title: Jahresziffer Prüfung
project31.title2: A Tool for Leap Year Calculation
project31.description: A simple C# console app practice project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project31.description2: The app checks whether an entered year is a leap year based on the mathematical rules for leap years.
project31.description3: The input is also validated, and appropriate feedback is provided in case of invalid input.
project31.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Jahresziffer Prüfung application

project32.title: Fizz Buzz
project32.title2: The FizzBuzz Algorithm as a Console App
project32.description: A simple C# console app practice project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development at Lutz + Grub Academy. It implements the 'Fizz Buzz' algorithm, a well-known group game for children to learn division in a playful way.
project32.description2: The program counts upwards and replaces every number divisible by three with 'fizz', every number divisible by five with 'buzz', and every number divisible by both three and five with 'fizzbuzz'.
project32.description3: The code was written entirely by me. The assignment only provided a general direction for what the practice project should achieve.
project32.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Fizz Buzz application

project33.title: Promillerechner
project33.title2: A Simulation for Calculating Blood Alcohol Level
project33.description: A simple C# console app practice project created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development.
project33.description2: The app calculates the estimated blood alcohol level based on the amount of beer consumed and the user's body weight.
project33.description3: The code was written independently by me. The assignment only provided a rough direction.

project34.title: Wetter Prüfung
project34.description: My first self-developed C# console project, created during my retraining as a Computer Science Expert: Software Development at Lutz + Grub Academy.
project34.description2: The app asks for the current weather condition ('sunny' or 'rainy') and the temperature, then provides recommendations based on that – for example, whether to wear a T-shirt or a jacket, and whether an umbrella is advisable.
project34.description3: The assignment was intentionally open-ended. I developed the app entirely on my own, from idea to code. This project helped me practice the basics of C#, logical thinking, and user interaction.
project34.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Wetter Prüfung application
